cases.reason: The framing parallel is an embedded curve, not an independently reoriented stationary link component. The wording leaves its auxiliary orientation implicit. concern.concern: The Statement instructs: “cut B⁴ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface” and “do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face,” then calls the result the cyclic branched cover. Proof 3.1 nevertheless asserts that the cut sheets form the local model w↦w^q and that a meridian moves cyclically through all q sheets. Taken literally as cut-face gluing, the specified chain leaves terminal faces unmatched and does not establish that local branched-cover model. A pushed-in surface also has codimension two, so the cutting hypersurface and its faces require specification. The standard q−1 interfaces in a handle or thickened-surface construction must be distinguished from q cyclic cut-face identifications. Proof 1.1 assumes the cut pieces are 4-balls and obtains the handles without supplying this distinction; the chain diagram does not resolve it. The matrix itself is corroborated by Przytycki–Yasuhara §3, printed p. 13 (https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0111203), which attributes the surgery construction to Akbulut–Kirby. I could not extract a readable argument from the retrieved Akbulut–Kirby PDF, so I do not claim to have checked that original construction. The literal construction and its claimed boundary remain unsupported as written.
